headline: Keep {arm:September}: both candidates hold Kairo in character less often, and at this run's unnamed provider routing both also cost more per reply.
lede: {arm:qwen3.8-flash}'s character pass rate is clearly lower than {arm:September}'s and {arm:1017}'s drop is not told apart from zero, so neither beats the control on what was asked. Only a candidate that kept character better would change the call; a named provider pricing one below {arm:September} would remove the cost half of the reason, not the character half.

caveats.material_if: Only if the judge marks the candidates' replies down for style rather than character. Then the call would rest on cost alone, which is measured at a routing no arm names and which an earlier round contradicted for {arm:qwen3.8-flash}; it would hold only as the status-quo default until the costs are repriced.

caveats.label: Costs belong to an unnamed provider routing
caveats.material_if: Only if a named provider prices a candidate at or below {arm:September}. Then the cost half of the call falls and it rests on character, where {arm:qwen3.8-flash} is still clearly worse and {arm:1017} is not shown better.
Only if a different character aspect would have been chosen before the results, and that aspect showed a candidate ahead of {arm:September}.
Only if the intended baseline was not the model in production today; {arm:September} is that model.
Only if some setting besides the model moved between arms; each arm's recorded settings change the model alone.

decision.text: Keep {arm:September} (the control) as Kairo's persona model. Its character pass rate is {pass_rate.September}, the highest of the three, at {cost_per_1k.September|usd_per_1k} production cost, the lowest of the three at this run's routing, which no arm names.

{arm:qwen3.8-flash}: its character pass rate is down {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points (interval {reading.qwen3.8-flash.interval|interval}) and at this run's routing it costs {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} more. {arm:1017}: its pass-rate drop of {reading.1017.change|abs|pts} points is not told apart from zero, it holds character less often by {contrast.1017.persona.holds_character.delta|abs|pts} points, and at this run's routing it costs {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} more.

The weakest margin is {weakest.arm}'s pass rate against the margin on character adherence: its family-corrected interval reaches {weakest.value|pts} against a line at {weakest.threshold|pts}, {weakest.margin|abs|pts} points short of it; on the {reading.qwen3.8-flash.level} reading its drop reaches {flip_margin.qwen3.8-flash|abs|pts} points, the figure the margin control uses. Neither moves the call, since {arm:September} is kept either way. This run contradicts the earlier finding that {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lowers production cost; no arm names its provider, so whether the routing changed is unknown. {arm:1017} spent {reasoning_ratio.1017} of its output reasoning against {reasoning_ratio.September} for {arm:September}, so its figures are not at matched reasoning.

Keep {arm:September} now. Rework how every model handles off-lane asks, where both candidates fall furthest behind, and rerun all three arms; in parallel, calibrate the judge and reprice the arms at named providers.

claims.text: Both candidates hold Kairo in character less often than {arm:September}: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} is clearly worse on the character pass rate, by {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.passed.delta|abs|pts} points, and {arm:1017} is down {contrast.1017.passed.delta|abs|pts} points, not told apart from zero, while the judged holds-character rate is lower for both. Each drop stays inside the declared {aspects.character adherence (v2).margin|int}-point margin.

evidence.caption: Change against {arm:September} on the character pass rate and the judged holds-character rate, paired over {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.passed.n_cases|int} cases, at the family-corrected {family.level} level; the shaded band is the margin. {arm:1017} reasoned on a smaller share of its output than {arm:September}, which could pull its character figures either way; {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lost {scoreboard.qwen3.8-flash.lost|words} trials to the harness, too few to move its rate.

claims.text: At this run's routing, which no arm names, both candidates cost more to run: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} by {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} and {arm:1017} by {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k}, each interval clear of zero.

evidence.caption: Paired production-cost gap against {arm:September}, at the family-corrected {family.level} level. Some trials reported no cost ({cost.unreported.September.missing|int} for {arm:September}, {cost.unreported.qwen3.8-flash.missing|int} for {arm:qwen3.8-flash}, {cost.unreported.1017.missing|int} for {arm:1017}). Filling {arm:September}'s at its own p95 puts its mean at {cost.unreported.September.at_p95|usd_per_1k}; counting the candidates' as free puts theirs at {cost.unreported.qwen3.8-flash.free|usd_per_1k} and {cost.unreported.1017.free|usd_per_1k}, so the order holds even at that worst case. {arm:1017} reasons less than {arm:September}; matching its reasoning would likely widen its cost gap.

claims.text: Off-lane asks are where both candidates fall furthest behind on the judged holds-character rate ({strata.off_lane.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character.vs_control|pts} points for {arm:qwen3.8-flash}, {strata.off_lane.1017.persona.holds_character.vs_control|pts} for {arm:1017}), and where {arm:September} is weakest too among strata of ten cases or more, at {strata.off_lane.September.persona.holds_character.mean}.

evidence.caption: Each candidate's judged holds-character rate minus {arm:September}'s, in the eight largest strata; uncorrected and exploratory, so read the off-lane gap as a lead. {arm:1017}'s rows carry its lower reasoning share, which could move them either way.
Each arm's judged holds-character rate on off-lane asks, over {strata.off_lane.n_cases|int} cases.

claims.text: Read from the few off-lane failures the snapshot kept, they fall into two patterns: brushing the ask off in voice and then slipping out of it (the first and third cards, from {arm:1017} and {arm:September}), and answering the non-music request that should have been declined (the second card, from {arm:qwen3.8-flash}). Among the other kept failures, answering the ask appears for all three models, so neither pattern belongs to one model alone.

evidence.caption: One kept off-lane failure per arm, the control's among them. The snapshot kept {count.examples.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|words} of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|int} off-lane failures for {arm:September}, {count.examples.character adherence (v2).qwen3.8-flash.off_lane|words} of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).qwen3.8-flash.off_lane|int} for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and {count.examples.character adherence (v2).1017.off_lane|words} of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).1017.off_lane|int} for {arm:1017}, so the patterns are a reading of a sample, not a count.

explore.binds: Whether each candidate counts as acceptable on character
explore.outcome: Read on the {reading.qwen3.8-flash.level} readings, {arm:1017}'s verdict turns at a margin of {flip_margin.1017|abs|pts} points and {arm:qwen3.8-flash}'s at {flip_margin.qwen3.8-flash|abs|pts}. Keeping {arm:September} holds at every margin, since no margin makes a candidate better than the control.

next.text: Rework the AI-lane directive for off-lane asks and rerun all three arms on the same cases.
next.settles: Whether the off-lane failure every model shares can be fixed, and whether a candidate then keeps character as well as {arm:September}.

next.text: Calibrate the character judge against human ratings of the same replies.
next.settles: Whether the holds-character drops are real or a judge preference; it would turn the main open caveat into evidence.

next.text: Confirm the provider each arm was served by and reprice all three, {arm:qwen3.8-flash} against the earlier round above all.
next.settles: Whether the cost half of the call stands: whether this run's higher production cost or the earlier finding that it lowers cost is the one that holds.

next.text: If {arm:1017} stays of interest, rerun it at matched reasoning on {settle.passed.character adherence (v2).1017.September.cases_needed_80|int} cases per arm. That is more than the suite's {cases|int} cases, so new cases must be written; more repeats of today's cases would not narrow an interval that counts cases.
next.settles: Whether its pass-rate drop of {settle.passed.character adherence (v2).1017.September.difference|abs|pts} points is real, four times in five if today's estimate holds.

method.text: {cases|int} cases, each run {repeats|words} times per arm; intervals count cases, not trials.

Readings against the control are at {reading.qwen3.8-flash.level}. Contrasts are paired over cases and corrected together by Holm's method across {family.family_size|int} comparisons, each interval at {family.level}. The weakest margin is read on the corrected interval, the margin control on the readings. Stratum breakdowns are uncorrected.

A candidate may be up to {aspects.character adherence (v2).margin|int} points worse on the character pass rate and still count as acceptable; set after the results, and the call holds at every margin.
The floor on the rate drop reads the character pass rate for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} but the judged holds-character rate for {arm:1017}, a mismatch; both held, and the call rests on neither floor.
One model judged every dimension, with no calibration ratings, so its tier is undetermined.

Production cost per 1,000 replies, replicating what production pays; no arm names its provider, so the routing behind each cost is unknown and the cost order is this run's, not the models' own. Token counts and model-call counts were not reported.
Latency, because every run executed beside others. Whether the simulated user's request settings varied was not recorded on every run.
